 VividFrame GPU
 Any source. One real-time GPU enhancement pipeline. 

VividFrame GPU is a Windows video player and capture enhancer that runs one real-time GPU pipeline over everything you watch — local video files, capture cards, screen capture and console or PC streaming — layering AI super resolution, noise reduction, HDR, frame generation and colour tools on top of the picture as it plays, rendered natively in DirectX 12.

[download-url]: 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 🎯 Why

Low-resolution files, noisy captures and 60 FPS consoles hit the same wall: the picture you actually see is the picture your source delivers. Post-processing after the fact is slow and disconnected from playback. VividFrame GPU moves the whole enhancement stack onto the GPU and into the player itself — the source feeds one chain, and every frame you see comes out sharpened, cleaned, HDR-mapped and, when you want it, frame-multiplied, with no separate rendering step and no offline wait.

 🆚 Without / With

 Without With 
 --- --- 
 Watch a low-res file as-is, or run a slow offline upscaler and wait for the export Play the file directly with AI super resolution and layered noise reduction applied in real time 
 A separate HDR tool, a separate frame interpolator, a separate player One chain covers super resolution, RTX Video HDR, frame generation, colour and anti-aliasing 
 Console games capped at the console's own picture quality Stream a PS5 or a PC host and enhance the incoming picture live on the way to your screen 
 Re-encode every clip you want improved Enhance live for viewing, then export exactly what you tuned to MP4/MKV when you want to keep it 

 🚀 Quick Start

1. Save the portable ZIP for your GPU vendor — an NVIDIA or an AMD build — into a new folder with the Download button at the top.
2. powershell Expand-Archive -Path ".\vividframe-gpu-win64-portable.zip" -DestinationPath ".\vividframe-gpu" 
3. Run the application executable from the extracted folder and start with all effects off — check picture and sound first.
4. powershell .\vividframe-gpu\vividframe-gpu.exe 
5. Enable effects one at a time — super resolution, noise reduction, HDR, frame generation — and check GPU load as each layer goes in.

 Note: Windows 11 x64 and DirectX 12 are required. Qt runtimes ship inside the package; GPU and capture drivers are installed separately. High resolution, stacked NR layers and frame generation raise GPU/VRAM demands.

 Tip: extract into a new writable folder on each version change and copy only your saved user data — do not overwrite a new package with old settings files or mixed runtimes.

 ✨ Features

- Upscale video in real time with NVIDIA RTX Video Super Resolution and selectable DLSS/XeSS/FSR backends.
- Denoise with up to four independent NR layers, each with its own internal resolution, strength and parameters.
- Restore HDR with RTX Video HDR and wide-gamut handling for SDR sources.
- Generate frames on the fly with a supported frame-generation backend and multiplier.
- Stream from a PS5, a Sunshine host on a PC, an Xbox (experimental), a capture card or the screen itself.
- Edit effects as an ordered layer list or as an executable node chain — with separate presets and sessions for each.
- Export the enhanced picture to MP4/MKV from an editable queue with trimming and multi-track audio and subtitles.

 ⚙️ How it works

QML renders the interface while a native D3D12 pipeline renders the video: every source — files, capture card, PS5, PC host, Xbox, screen — becomes a frame stream, which flows through a shared enhancement graph of NR layers, a single SR stage, colour tools, HDR and optional final frame generation, then presents live in a native DirectX 12 window or hands off to the offline export queue. List and node modes share that one engine, so what you tune is what you export.

 🕹️ Usage

1. Movie night, upgraded. Open an old 1080p file, enable super resolution and two NR layers, and watch it sharpened live — then send it to the export queue if you want a permanent copy.
2. Console on the big screen. Connect a capture card or PS5 Remote Play, match the signal format, and stack SR, HDR and frame generation on the incoming picture for a smoother, brighter feed.
3. PC streaming. Point the player at a Sunshine host, connect, and treat the streamed game like any other source — enhance it, screenshot it with F7, or record the processed picture with F8.

 🛠️ Configuration

 Setting What it controls 
 --- --- 
 SR model Per-layer super-resolution family, saved with presets and sessions 
 NR layers Up to four layers with independent resolution, strength and protection regions 
 Frame generation Backend and multiplier, cadence and display-sync options 
 Colour Basic adjustments, curves, mixer, wheels, LUTs and colour presets 
 Shortcuts Hotkeys for Home, screenshots, recording and control lock — configurable 
 OBS Game Capture Compatibility switch with restart confirmation for capturing video into OBS 
 Startup Resume last source at startup and configurable startup page 
 GPU Compute-GPU selection and RTX DLSS performance mode 

 🧯 Troubleshooting / FAQ

 Everything stutters with all effects on. Start with effects off and enable them one at a time; high resolution, layered NR and frame generation all raise GPU and VRAM load.

 An overlay or monitoring tool conflicts with the picture. With RTSS-style overlays running, use software interface rendering and check the overlay's hooking option — or switch your capture method to Window Capture for the full interface.

 Export fails from Node mode. Node mode does not support offline export; verify the chain in List mode and export from there — graphs are not silently converted.

 After an upgrade the app misbehaves. Extract the new package into a fresh folder and copy only your user data across; stale runtimes and mixed libraries from an in-place overlay are a known trouble source.

 Where are my settings? Presets, sessions and custom paths
